title: Differentiation under an integral with a locally dominated Frechet derivative
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], let $(X,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $E,H$ be real Banach spaces. Let $F:H\times X\to E$, $F':H\times X\to\mathcal L_{\mathbf R}(H,E)$, $x_0\in H$, and let $s\subset H$ be a neighbourhood of $x_0$, where $\mathcal L_{\mathbf R}(H,E)$ denotes bounded real-linear maps with operator norm. Suppose $F(x,\cdot)$ is almost-everywhere strongly measurable for all $x$ in some neighbourhood of $x_0$, $F(x_0,\cdot)$ is Bochner integrable, and $F'(x_0,\cdot)$ is almost-everywhere strongly measurable. Suppose there is a Bochner integrable real function $g:X\to\mathbf R$ such that, for almost every $y$, simultaneously for every $x\in s$, the map $F(\cdot,y)$ has Frechet derivative $F'(x,y)$ at $x$ and $\|F'(x,y)\|\leq g(y)$. Then $$x\longmapsto\int_X F(x,y)\,d\mu(y)$$ has Frechet derivative $$\int_X F'(x_0,y)\,d\mu(y)$$ at $x_0$.
